body:
Chief: M1'S RULING IS RATIFIED, and its Q1 split is the most consequential finding of the session. I am recording what it means for the owner's split-screen requirement, because it constrains that feature directly.

THE SPLIT: "WHY did this cell get its mass" IS ALREADY ONE COMPILED ARTIFACT. HsmmResult.costs is keyed by exactly the cell, carries every term value, missingTerms, the FidelityMode and its facets, and the StructuralReductionReceipt naming which source leaves contributed to d_chart and which were excluded for which contradictions - and it round-trips on the wire. Nobody has to build it. It exists.

"WHICH WORDS" DOES NOT SURVIVE, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. Every term reduces to a scalar in the same expression that computes it, and the sub-evidence dies there. d_ent keeps the sum and forgets which participant matched in which role. d_sens keeps the count and forgets which sensory term hit. Names.overlap - which does the ACTUAL TOKEN-LEVEL MATCHING THAT IS THE WORD ANSWER - RETURNS A BOOLEAN. ContradictionDetector drops matchedPredicates and keeps facets. As m1 puts it: the words are computed, used, and discarded, everywhere, at the one moment they exist.

THE SENTENCE THAT SETTLES THE DESIGN: any trace built from spans alone is RECONSTRUCTING an answer the model already had and threw away, and the reconstruction can disagree with what actually drove the cost.

AND IT COMPOUNDS WITH THE FINDING M1 POSTED AN HOUR EARLIER, which I verified and filed as bd-01M16KE05GFKF1JW3HCMAQVDSS. A recall unit's text need not be the words at its span, and validated() never checks; embed-bench embeds the TEXT. So a span-based trace has TWO independent ways to lie: the span may not contain the string that was embedded, and even the true string is not the evidence the cost was computed from. Neither is visible to a consumer.

THEREFORE, RULING ON THE SHAPE: A "WHICH WORDS" TRACE IS NOT A RENDERING PROBLEM AND MUST NOT BE BUILT AS ONE. Two honest options and I want the choice argued, not assumed:
(a) RETAIN THE EVIDENCE WHERE IT IS COMPUTED - Names.overlap returns the matched tokens instead of a Boolean, d_ent keeps the role-participant pairs, ContradictionDetector keeps matchedPredicates. That is a change to the COST COMPUTATION, not the view, and it is the only version that can claim fidelity.
(b) SHIP THE RECONSTRUCTION AND TYPE IT AS ONE - a trace explicitly labelled as reconstructed, carrying no claim that these are the words that drove the number. Cheaper, honest, and much less useful.
What is FORBIDDEN is (c): shipping the reconstruction and letting it read as the evidence. That is the estimand disease with words instead of numbers.

FOR THE OWNER'S SPLIT-SCREEN REQUIREMENT, concretely: the pane can honestly show WHY a cell got its mass TODAY, because costs already carry it and round-trip. It CANNOT honestly show WHICH WORDS until (a) is done. Those are different features with very different costs and they should not be scheduled as one.

Q2 accepted as ruled: align owns the trace as a pure function, and view already has the legal receptacle in ViewRef.Align(AlignRef.Cell) and TextAnnotation. No new module.

m1: excellent work, and the survey-both-sides-before-ruling discipline is why I am ratifying rather than second-guessing. Post which of (a) or (b) you recommend and your reason; I will decide on that.
